description: Provenance-first English maritime MCQ benchmark for CPT model evaluation.

items.question: Under the COLREGs, what must every vessel maintain at all times?
choices: A. A proper lookout by sight and hearing
B. A visual watch only
C. A radio watch only
D. A radar watch only, with no visual lookout
items.correct_text: A proper lookout by sight and hearing
items.evidence: Rule 5 requires a proper lookout by sight and hearing as well as by all available means.

items.question: Which factors must be taken into account when determining a safe speed?
choices: A. Port dues and pilotage fees
B. Visibility, traffic, and handling
C. Crew nationality and rank
D. Cargo value, fuel cost, and schedule
items.correct_text: Visibility, traffic, and handling
items.evidence: Rule 6 lists visibility, traffic density, manoeuvrability, background lights, sea state, and draft.

items.question: What should a vessel do when there is any doubt whether risk of collision exists?
choices: A. Wait for the other vessel to sound
B. Maintain course until visual contact
C. Reduce speed only in fog
D. Assume that risk of collision exists
items.correct_text: Assume that risk of collision exists
items.evidence: Rule 7(d): if there is any doubt, such risk shall be deemed to exist.

items.question: Which description best matches a course of action taken to avoid collision?
choices: A. Delayed until the other vessel responds
B. Small and gradual, to avoid alarming the other vessel
C. Positive, timely, and consistent with seamanship
D. Always to port, regardless of the situation
items.correct_text: Positive, timely, and consistent with seamanship
items.evidence: Rule 8(a): any action shall be positive, made in ample time, and with due regard to seamanship.

items.question: In a narrow channel, where should a vessel keep?
choices: A. As near to the centreline as is safe and practicable
B. As near to the outer limit on her port side as is safe and practicable
C. Anywhere in the channel, provided speed is reduced
D. As near to starboard as safe and practicable
items.correct_text: As near to starboard as safe and practicable
items.evidence: Rule 9(a): a vessel proceeding along a narrow channel shall keep as near to the outer limit on her starboard side as is safe and practicable.

items.question: In a narrow channel, a vessel of less than 20 metres or a sailing vessel shall not impede which vessel?
choices: A. A vessel engaged in fishing
B. A vessel that can only use the channel
C. A vessel of less than 20 metres in length
D. A sailing vessel under oars
items.correct_text: A vessel that can only use the channel
items.evidence: Rule 9(b): small vessels and sailing vessels shall not impede a vessel that can safely navigate only within the channel.

items.question: A vessel using a traffic separation scheme shall normally proceed in which direction?
choices: A. In the separation zone, to keep clear of traffic
B. On either side of the lane, if visibility is good
C. In the lane, following the traffic flow
D. Against the flow, if the vessel is small
items.correct_text: In the lane, following the traffic flow
items.evidence: Rule 10(b)(i): a vessel using a traffic lane shall proceed in the general direction of traffic flow.

items.question: When a vessel has to cross a traffic lane, how should she cross?
choices: A. As slowly as possible, to avoid collision
B. Only at the lane's termination points
C. At right angles to the traffic flow
D. At an angle of 45 degrees to the flow
items.correct_text: At right angles to the traffic flow
items.evidence: Rule 10(c): a vessel shall cross a traffic lane at right angles to the general direction of traffic flow.

items.question: A vessel shall NOT use the inshore traffic zone when which condition applies?
choices: A. She is a sailing vessel
B. She is engaged in fishing
C. She can safely use the lane
D. Her destination is within the zone
items.correct_text: She can safely use the lane
items.evidence: Rule 10(d): the inshore traffic zone shall not be used when the vessel can safely use the adjacent traffic lane.

items.question: How long does an overtaking vessel remain the give-way vessel?
choices: A. Until the other vessel reduces speed
B. Until she is finally past and clear
C. Until both vessels are in visual contact
D. Until her bow has passed the other vessel
items.correct_text: Until she is finally past and clear
items.evidence: Rule 13(a): the overtaking vessel shall keep out of the way until she is finally past and clear.

items.question: What should a vessel do if she is in doubt whether she is overtaking another vessel?
choices: A. Sound one short blast and maintain course
B. Assume she is overtaking and give way
C. Assume that she is crossing and stand on
D. Wait for the other vessel to signal
items.correct_text: Assume she is overtaking and give way
items.evidence: Rule 13(b): if in doubt, the vessel shall assume she is overtaking and act accordingly.

items.question: When two power-driven vessels meet head-on, what should they do?
choices: A. Both alter course to starboard and pass port-to-port
B. Both alter course to port and pass starboard-to-starboard
C. Both stop engines and drift
D. The smaller vessel gives way
items.correct_text: Both alter course to starboard and pass port-to-port
items.evidence: Rule 14(a): each vessel shall alter course to starboard so that they pass port-to-port.

items.question: In a crossing situation, which power-driven vessel must give way?
choices: A. The vessel carrying dangerous cargo
B. The vessel with the greater speed
C. The vessel with the other on starboard
D. The vessel that has the other on her port side
items.correct_text: The vessel with the other on starboard
items.evidence: Rule 15: the vessel which has the other on her starboard side shall keep out of the way.

items.question: What action must the give-way vessel take?
choices: A. Take early and substantial action to keep well clear
B. Make a small course change at the last moment
C. Sound five short blasts and stop
D. Maintain course and speed until the stand-on vessel acts
items.correct_text: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear
items.evidence: Rule 16: the give-way vessel shall take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

items.question: What must the stand-on vessel initially do?
choices: A. Stop engines and wait
B. Keep her course and speed
C. Alter course to port immediately
D. Increase speed to pass ahead
items.correct_text: Keep her course and speed
items.evidence: Rule 17(a)(i): the stand-on vessel shall keep her course and speed.

items.question: When may the stand-on vessel take action to avoid collision?
choices: A. Only if the vessels are in restricted visibility
B. Only after a collision has occurred
C. When the give-way vessel is not acting
D. Only if the give-way vessel sounds one short blast
items.correct_text: When the give-way vessel is not acting
items.evidence: Rule 17(a)(ii): the stand-on vessel may act as soon as it becomes apparent the give-way vessel is not acting.

items.question: A power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of which vessel?
choices: A. A vessel moored to a buoy
B. A vessel at anchor
C. A vessel underway with a pilot on board
D. A vessel not under command
items.correct_text: A vessel not under command
items.evidence: Rule 18(a)(i): a power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of a vessel not under command.

items.question: A sailing vessel underway shall keep out of the way of which vessel?
choices: A. A vessel at anchor
B. A vessel moored to a buoy
C. A power-driven vessel underway
D. A vessel engaged in fishing
items.correct_text: A vessel engaged in fishing
items.evidence: Rule 18(a)(ii): a sailing vessel shall keep out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing.

items.question: What should a vessel do in restricted visibility?
choices: A. Reduce speed and ready the engines
B. Stop engines and drift until visibility improves
C. Maintain speed and switch on all deck lights
D. Increase speed to clear the area quickly
items.correct_text: Reduce speed and ready the engines
items.evidence: Rule 19(b): every vessel shall proceed at a safe speed adapted to the prevailing circumstances and visibility.

items.question: In restricted visibility, what alteration should be avoided for a vessel forward of the beam?
choices: A. A change in engine telegraph
B. An alteration of course to starboard
C. A reduction of speed
D. An alteration of course to port
items.correct_text: An alteration of course to port
items.evidence: Rule 19(d)(i): avoid altering course to port for a vessel forward of the beam, other than for a vessel being overtaken.

items.question: What is the arc of visibility of a masthead light?
choices: A. 225 degrees
B. 112.5 degrees
C. 135 degrees
D. 360 degrees
items.correct_text: 225 degrees
items.evidence: Rule 21(a): a masthead light shows over an arc of 225 degrees.

items.question: What colours are the sidelights of a vessel?
choices: A. White on both sides
B. Yellow on both sides
C. Red on the port side and green on the starboard side
D. Green on the port side and red on the starboard side
items.correct_text: Red on the port side and green on the starboard side
items.evidence: Rule 21(b): sidelights are red on the port side and green on the starboard side.

items.question: What is the arc of visibility of a sternlight?
choices: A. 225 degrees
B. 135 degrees
C. 360 degrees
D. 112.5 degrees
items.correct_text: 135 degrees
items.evidence: Rule 21(c): a sternlight shows over an arc of 135 degrees.

items.question: What is an all-round light?
choices: A. An unbroken 360-degree arc
B. A light showing an arc of 225 degrees
C. A light showing two arcs of 112.5 degrees
D. A light showing an arc of 135 degrees
items.correct_text: An unbroken 360-degree arc
items.evidence: Rule 21(e): an all-round light shows an unbroken arc of 360 degrees.

items.question: Which lights must a power-driven vessel of less than 50 metres show when underway at night?
choices: A. A masthead light, sidelights, and a sternlight
B. A masthead light, a sternlight, and an all-round red light
C. Two masthead lights, sidelights, and a sternlight
D. Sidelights and a sternlight only
items.correct_text: A masthead light, sidelights, and a sternlight
items.evidence: Rule 23(a): a power-driven vessel underway shows a masthead light, sidelights, and a sternlight; a second masthead light is optional below 50 m.

items.question: Which lights may a power-driven vessel of less than 12 metres show when underway?
choices: A. An all-round white light and sidelights
B. A red over green all-round light
C. A white over red all-round light
D. Two masthead lights and a sternlight at the foremast
items.correct_text: An all-round white light and sidelights
items.evidence: Rule 23(d): a power-driven vessel of less than 12 m may show an all-round white light and sidelights.

items.question: A power-driven vessel towing a tow of less than 200 metres must show which lights?
choices: A. Three masthead lights in a vertical line
B. Two masthead lights in a vertical line
C. Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
D. One masthead light and two sternlights
items.correct_text: Two masthead lights in a vertical line
items.evidence: Rule 24(a): a towing vessel shows two masthead lights in a vertical line; three if the tow exceeds 200 m.

items.question: Which lights must a sailing vessel underway show at night?
choices: A. Sidelights and a sternlight
B. Two masthead lights and a sternlight at the foremast
C. A masthead light, sidelights, and a sternlight
D. An all-round white light only
items.correct_text: Sidelights and a sternlight
items.evidence: Rule 25(a): a sailing vessel underway shows sidelights and a sternlight, and may show red over green at the masthead.

items.question: A vessel engaged in trawling must show which lights?
choices: A. A white light over a red light
B. A red light over a white light
C. Two red lights in a vertical line
D. A green light over a white light
items.correct_text: A green light over a white light
items.evidence: Rule 26(b): a trawler shows a green light over a white light, all-round.

items.question: A vessel not under command must show which lights at night?
choices: A. Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
B. Two all-round green lights in a vertical line
C. Red over white over red all-round lights
D. Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
items.correct_text: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
items.evidence: Rule 27(a): a vessel not under command shows two all-round red lights in a vertical line, and two black balls by day.

items.question: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre must show which lights at night?
choices: A. White over red over white all-round lights
B. Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
C. Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
D. Red over white over red all-round lights
items.correct_text: Red over white over red all-round lights
items.evidence: Rule 27(b): a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre shows red over white over red all-round lights.

items.question: A vessel constrained by her draft must show which lights at night?
choices: A. Red over white over red all-round lights
B. Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
C. Three all-round red lights
D. A green light over a white light
items.correct_text: Three all-round red lights
items.evidence: Rule 28: a vessel constrained by her draft shows three all-round red lights in a vertical line, and a cylinder by day.

items.question: A pilot vessel on pilotage duty must show which lights at night?
choices: A. White over red all-round lights
B. Red over white all-round lights
C. Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
D. Green over white all-round lights
items.correct_text: White over red all-round lights
items.evidence: Rule 29(a): a pilot vessel shows white over red all-round lights, and sidelights and a sternlight when underway.

items.question: A vessel of less than 50 metres at anchor must show which light?
choices: A. Two all-round white lights in a vertical line
B. Two all-round white lights, one forward and one aft
C. One all-round white light where it can best be seen
D. A red light over a white light
items.correct_text: One all-round white light where it can best be seen
items.evidence: Rule 30(b): a vessel under 50 m at anchor shows one all-round white light where it can best be seen.

items.question: A vessel aground must show which additional lights at night?
choices: A. Red over white over red all-round lights
B. Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
C. Two all-round green lights in a vertical line
D. Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
items.correct_text: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
items.evidence: Rule 30(d): a vessel aground shows the anchor lights plus two all-round red lights in a vertical line.

items.question: How long is a short blast on the whistle?
choices: A. About thirty seconds
B. About four to six seconds
C. About ten seconds
D. About one second
items.correct_text: About one second
items.evidence: Rule 32(a): a short blast is a blast of about one second's duration.

items.question: How long is a prolonged blast on the whistle?
choices: A. Four to six seconds
B. Ten to twelve seconds
C. One second
D. Two to three seconds
items.correct_text: Four to six seconds
items.evidence: Rule 32(b): a prolonged blast is a blast of from four to six seconds' duration.

items.question: What does one short blast mean when vessels are in sight of one another?
choices: A. I intend to overtake you on your port side
B. I am altering my course to starboard
C. I am altering my course to port
D. I am operating astern propulsion
items.correct_text: I am altering my course to starboard
items.evidence: Rule 34(a): one short blast means 'I am altering my course to starboard'.

items.question: What do two short blasts mean when vessels are in sight of one another?
choices: A. I am altering my course to starboard
B. I am altering my course to port
C. I intend to overtake you on your starboard side
D. I am operating astern propulsion
items.correct_text: I am altering my course to port
items.evidence: Rule 34(a): two short blasts mean 'I am altering my course to port'.

items.question: What do three short blasts mean when vessels are in sight of one another?
choices: A. I am operating astern propulsion
B. I am altering my course to starboard
C. I am in distress and require assistance
D. I am altering my course to port
items.correct_text: I am operating astern propulsion
items.evidence: Rule 34(a): three short blasts mean 'I am operating astern propulsion'.

items.question: Which signal indicates an intention to overtake on the starboard side?
choices: A. One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts
B. Three short blasts
C. Two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
D. Two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts
items.correct_text: Two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
items.evidence: Rule 34(c)(i): two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast indicate overtaking on the starboard side.

items.question: Which signal indicates an intention to overtake on the port side?
choices: A. Two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
B. One prolonged blast followed by one short blast
C. Three short blasts
D. Two prolonged and two short blasts
items.correct_text: Two prolonged and two short blasts
items.evidence: Rule 34(c)(ii): two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts indicate overtaking on the port side.

items.question: In restricted visibility, what sound signal does a power-driven vessel make while underway?
choices: A. One prolonged blast at intervals of not more than two minutes
B. One prolonged blast at intervals of not more than ten minutes
C. Two prolonged blasts at intervals of not more than two minutes
D. Three short blasts at intervals of not more than one minute
items.correct_text: One prolonged blast at intervals of not more than two minutes
items.evidence: Rule 35(a): a power-driven vessel making way through the water sounds one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than two minutes.

items.question: In restricted visibility, what signal does a vessel stopped and making no way through the water make?
choices: A. Rapid ringing of the bell for five seconds
B. Two prolonged blasts, two seconds apart
C. Three short blasts
D. One prolonged blast and two short blasts
items.correct_text: Two prolonged blasts, two seconds apart
items.evidence: Rule 35(b): a vessel stopped and making no way sounds two prolonged blasts with about two seconds between them.

items.question: In restricted visibility, what signal does a vessel not under command make?
choices: A. Two prolonged blasts
B. One prolonged blast followed by three short blasts
C. One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts
D. Two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast
items.correct_text: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts
items.evidence: Rule 35(c): a vessel not under command, restricted in ability to manoeuvre, or constrained by draft sounds one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts.

items.question: In restricted visibility, what signal does an anchored vessel make?
choices: A. Two prolonged blasts at intervals of not more than two minutes
B. Rapid bell ringing for about five seconds each minute
C. One prolonged blast at intervals of not more than two minutes
D. Three short blasts at intervals of not more than one minute
items.correct_text: Rapid bell ringing for about five seconds each minute
items.evidence: Rule 35(g): an anchored vessel rings the bell rapidly for about five seconds at intervals of not more than one minute.

items.question: Which signals may a vessel use to attract the attention of another vessel?
choices: A. A continuous sound signal
B. A gun fired at intervals of one minute
C. A distress signal, if no other signal is available
D. A light or flare, but not a distress signal
items.correct_text: A light or flare, but not a distress signal
items.evidence: Rule 36: a vessel may use sound or light signals to attract attention, but shall not use a distress signal.

items.question: Where are the distress signals listed?
choices: A. In Annex V
B. In Annex IV
C. In Annex I
D. In Annex II
items.correct_text: In Annex IV
items.evidence: Rule 37 refers to the distress signals listed in Annex IV.

items.question: Which vessel shall not impede the passage of a power-driven vessel using a traffic separation scheme?
choices: A. A vessel of less than 20 metres
B. A vessel at anchor
C. A vessel engaged in fishing
D. A sailing vessel
items.correct_text: A vessel engaged in fishing
items.evidence: Rule 10(i): a vessel engaged in fishing shall not impede the passage of a power-driven vessel using a traffic lane.

items.question: A vessel constrained by her draft has priority over which vessel?
choices: A. A vessel restricted in ability to manoeuvre
B. A vessel not under command
C. A power-driven vessel underway
D. A vessel engaged in fishing
items.correct_text: A power-driven vessel underway
items.evidence: Rule 18: a vessel constrained by draft is given priority over power-driven vessels, sailing vessels, and fishing vessels, but not over NUC or RAM vessels.

items.question: What is the main purpose of the SOLAS Convention?
choices: A. To set maximum cargo rates for international shipping
B. To harmonise seafarer wage scales across flag States
C. To regulate commercial competition between shipowners
D. To set minimum safety standards for ships
items.correct_text: To set minimum safety standards for ships
items.evidence: SOLAS establishes minimum standards for the safety of life at sea through ship construction, equipment, and operation.

items.question: How do most SOLAS amendments enter into force?
choices: A. After a vote by the United Nations Security Council
B. By tacit acceptance unless enough States object
C. When the IMO Secretary-General signs them in person
D. Only after every flag State ratifies them individually
items.correct_text: By tacit acceptance unless enough States object
items.evidence: Article VIII uses tacit acceptance: an amendment enters into force on a specified date unless it is rejected by the required number of Parties.

items.question: How long is a Passenger Ship Safety Certificate valid?
choices: A. 60 months
B. 24 months
C. 6 months
D. 12 months
items.correct_text: 12 months
items.evidence: A Passenger Ship Safety Certificate is valid for a period not exceeding 12 months.

items.question: What is the maximum validity of a Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate?
choices: A. 5 years
B. 1 year
C. 2 years
D. 10 years
items.correct_text: 5 years
items.evidence: A Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate is valid for a period not exceeding five years.

items.question: When must the annual survey of a cargo ship normally be carried out?
choices: A. Within thirty days before the certificate expires
B. Only during the first year after the ship is built
C. Within three months of the certificate anniversary
D. At any time during the five-year certificate period
items.correct_text: Within three months of the certificate anniversary
items.evidence: The annual survey is carried out within three months before or after the anniversary date of the certificate.

items.question: How often must fire drills be conducted on a ship?
choices: A. At least once every month
B. At least once every week
C. At least once every three months
D. At least once every six months
items.correct_text: At least once every month
items.evidence: Each fire drill shall be conducted at intervals not exceeding one month.

items.question: How often must abandon ship drills be conducted?
choices: A. At least once every three months
B. At least once every week
C. At least once every month
D. At least once every six months
items.correct_text: At least once every month
items.evidence: Each abandon ship drill shall be conducted at intervals not exceeding one month.

items.question: If more than 25% of the crew has not participated in an abandon ship drill, when must a drill be held?
choices: A. Before the next scheduled monthly drill
B. Before the ship next enters port
C. Within 7 days of the ship leaving port
D. Within 24 hours of leaving port
items.correct_text: Within 24 hours of leaving port
items.evidence: If more than 25% of the crew has not participated in the previous drill, a drill must be held within 24 hours of leaving port.

items.question: How often must each lifeboat be launched and manoeuvred in the water by its assigned crew?
choices: A. At least once every three months
B. At least once every month
C. At least once every six months
D. At least once every twelve months
items.correct_text: At least once every three months
items.evidence: Each lifeboat shall be launched and manoeuvred in the water by its assigned operating crew at least once every three months.

items.question: How often must life-saving appliances be inspected?
choices: A. At least once every week
B. At least once every month
C. At least once every day
D. At least once every three months
items.correct_text: At least once every week
items.evidence: Life-saving appliances shall be inspected at least once a week to ensure they are complete and in good order.

items.question: What must be displayed before a ship proceeds to sea to inform persons of their emergency duties?
choices: A. A muster list
B. A bunker delivery note
C. A ballast water record book
D. A cargo securing manual
items.correct_text: A muster list
items.evidence: A muster list shall be displayed in conspicuous places throughout the ship before the ship proceeds to sea.

items.question: How many lifejackets must a cargo ship provide for persons on board?
choices: A. Two for every person on board
B. One per person, plus watchkeeper lifejackets
C. One for every two persons on board
D. Only for the crew, not for passengers
items.correct_text: One per person, plus watchkeeper lifejackets
items.evidence: A lifejacket shall be provided for every person on board, with additional lifejackets for persons on watch and at remotely located survival craft stations.

items.question: How many immersion suits must a cargo ship carry?
choices: A. One for every two persons on board
B. Only for the master and chief engineer
C. Two for every person on board
D. One per person, plus watchkeeper suits
items.correct_text: One per person, plus watchkeeper suits
items.evidence: An immersion suit shall be provided for every person on board, with additional suits for watchkeeping personnel.

items.question: What marking must each lifebuoy carry?
choices: A. The owner's name and the charterer's name
B. The ship's name and port of registry
C. The flag State and gross tonnage
D. The ship's IMO number and call sign
items.correct_text: The ship's name and port of registry
items.evidence: Lifebuoys shall be marked with the ship's name and port of registry.

items.question: What is the minimum rescue boat requirement for a cargo ship?
choices: A. At least one rescue boat
B. One rescue boat for every fifty persons
C. At least two rescue boats, one on each side
D. No rescue boat if lifeboats are fitted
items.correct_text: At least one rescue boat
items.evidence: Cargo ships shall carry at least one rescue boat, which may be a lifeboat provided it also meets the rescue boat requirements.

items.question: A cargo ship uses the free-fall lifeboat option. What capacity must that lifeboat have?
choices: A. Capacity for 50% of the persons on board
B. Capacity for 150% of the persons on board
C. Capacity for 100% of the persons on board
D. Capacity for 200% of the persons on board
items.correct_text: Capacity for 100% of the persons on board
items.evidence: The free-fall lifeboat alternative must accommodate not less than 100% of the total number of persons on board.

items.question: What is the minimum number of independently driven fire pumps required on a cargo ship?
choices: A. Two independently driven fire pumps
B. Three independently driven fire pumps
C. One independently driven fire pump
D. Four independently driven fire pumps
items.correct_text: Two independently driven fire pumps
items.evidence: At least two independently driven power pumps shall be provided, each capable of delivering the required fire main pressure.

items.question: Which cargo ships must have an emergency fire pump?
choices: A. Only passenger ships of any size
B. Cargo ships of 500 gross tonnage and above
C. Cargo ships of 100 gross tonnage and above
D. Only tankers of 10,000 gross tonnage and above
items.correct_text: Cargo ships of 500 gross tonnage and above
items.evidence: Cargo ships of 500 gross tonnage and above shall be provided with an emergency fire pump.

items.question: What fire main performance must a cargo ship's fire pumps provide?
choices: A. A water mist spray from every hydrant
B. Two jets from different hydrants
C. At least four jets from the same hydrant
D. At least one jet of water from any hydrant
items.correct_text: Two jets from different hydrants
items.evidence: The fire main shall be capable of delivering at least two jets of water from different hydrants at the required pressure.

items.question: Where must a duplicate fire control plan be stored?
choices: A. In the engine room control station
B. In a weathertight box outside the deckhouse
C. In the master's safe inside the deckhouse
D. In the ship's office next to the certificates
items.correct_text: In a weathertight box outside the deckhouse
items.evidence: A duplicate fire control plan shall be stored in a prominently marked weathertight enclosure outside the deckhouse for shore-side fire-fighting assistance.

items.question: What is the general requirement for means of escape from accommodation spaces?
choices: A. Escape routes may pass through the engine room
B. Two means of escape per restricted space
C. At least three means of escape from each cabin
D. At least one means of escape from each space
items.correct_text: Two means of escape per restricted space
items.evidence: At least two means of escape shall be provided from each restricted space or group of spaces, with exceptions for small spaces.

items.question: Which cargo ships must have an emergency source of electrical power?
choices: A. Cargo ships of 100 gross tonnage and above
B. Only cargo ships carrying dangerous goods
C. Cargo ships of 500 gross tonnage and above
D. Only passenger ships of any size
items.correct_text: Cargo ships of 500 gross tonnage and above
items.evidence: Cargo ships of 500 gross tonnage and above shall be provided with an emergency source of electrical power.

items.question: When must the steering gear be tested before departure?
choices: A. Only after a steering gear failure has occurred
B. Within 24 hours before departure and once every six months
C. Within 12 hours before departure and every 3 months
D. Only when the ship changes flag State
items.correct_text: Within 12 hours before departure and every 3 months
items.evidence: Steering gear shall be tested within 12 hours before departure and at least once every three months.

items.question: How often must emergency steering drills be conducted?
choices: A. At least every twelve months
B. At least every six months
C. At least every month
D. At least every three months
items.correct_text: At least every three months
items.evidence: Emergency steering drills shall take place at least every three months.

items.question: Which ships must carry a voyage data recorder?
choices: A. All ships of 500 gross tonnage and above
B. Passenger ships and cargo ships of 3,000 GT+
C. Only passenger ships of any size
D. Only tankers of 10,000 gross tonnage and above
items.correct_text: Passenger ships and cargo ships of 3,000 GT+
items.evidence: A voyage data recorder is required on passenger ships and on cargo ships of 3,000 gross tonnage and above.

items.question: Under SOLAS V/19, which cargo ship on an international voyage must be fitted with AIS?
choices: A. A cargo ship of 300 gross tonnage and above
B. A cargo ship of 100 gross tonnage and above
C. A cargo ship of 1,000 gross tonnage and above
D. A cargo ship of 500 gross tonnage and above
items.correct_text: A cargo ship of 300 gross tonnage and above
items.evidence: AIS is required for cargo ships of 300 gross tonnage and above engaged on international voyages.

items.question: Which ships must be fitted with ECDIS under SOLAS V/19?
choices: A. All ships of 300 gross tonnage and above
B. Only tankers of 500 gross tonnage and above
C. Passenger ships 500 GT+ and cargo ships 3,000 GT+
D. Only passenger ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and above
items.correct_text: Passenger ships 500 GT+ and cargo ships 3,000 GT+
items.evidence: ECDIS is required for passenger ships of 500 gross tonnage and above and cargo ships of 3,000 gross tonnage and above.

items.question: What nautical publications must a ship carry for its intended voyage?
choices: A. Only a commercial world atlas
B. Only a set of tide tables from the last decade
C. Up-to-date charts and publications
D. Only the ship's certificate of registry
items.correct_text: Up-to-date charts and publications
items.evidence: Nautical charts and publications such as sailing directions, lists of lights, notices to mariners, and tide tables shall be adequate and up to date for the intended voyage.

items.question: What must the master do on encountering dangerous ice or a derelict?
choices: A. Alter course without informing anyone
B. Record it in the Oil Record Book only
C. Wait until the next port to report it
D. Send a danger message to nearby ships
items.correct_text: Send a danger message to nearby ships
items.evidence: The master of a ship encountering dangerous ice, a derelict, or another danger shall send a danger message to ships in the vicinity and to the appropriate authority.

items.question: What is the master's obligation when a distress message is received?
choices: A. Continue the voyage if the cargo is perishable
B. Ask the owner for permission before assisting
C. Wait for a warship to take charge of the rescue
D. Proceed at all speed to assist
items.correct_text: Proceed at all speed to assist
items.evidence: The master of a ship at sea receiving a distress message is bound to proceed with all speed to the assistance of persons in distress.

items.question: What must be provided for pilot transfer arrangements?
choices: A. A deck chair and a heaving line
B. SOLAS-compliant pilot transfer rigging
C. A pilot hoist without any certification
D. A temporary rope ladder of any length
items.correct_text: SOLAS-compliant pilot transfer rigging
items.evidence: Pilot transfer arrangements shall be rigged and used in accordance with SOLAS and IMO standards, including the pilot ladder requirements.

items.question: What must a cargo ship have before loading cargo units?
choices: A. An approved cargo securing manual
B. A bunker delivery note only
C. A passenger ship safety certificate
D. A grain loading certificate only
items.correct_text: An approved cargo securing manual
items.evidence: Cargo units shall be loaded, stowed, and secured throughout the voyage in accordance with an approved cargo securing manual.

items.question: What does the International Grain Code govern?
choices: A. The carriage of livestock on deck
B. The loading of containers on bulk carriers
C. The transport of nuclear fuel flasks
D. Safe stowage and securing of grain
items.correct_text: Safe stowage and securing of grain
items.evidence: The International Grain Code sets requirements for the safe stowage and securing of grain cargoes.

items.question: How must dangerous goods in packaged form be carried?
choices: A. Under the International Grain Code
B. Under the Polar Code only
C. In accordance with the IMDG Code
D. Under the IMSBC Code only
items.correct_text: In accordance with the IMDG Code
items.evidence: Dangerous goods in packaged form shall be carried in accordance with the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code.

items.question: Which certificate is required for a ship operating in polar waters?
choices: A. A Nuclear Ship Safety Certificate
B. A High-Speed Craft Certificate
C. A Passenger Ship Safety Certificate
D. A Polar Ship Certificate
items.correct_text: A Polar Ship Certificate
items.evidence: Ships operating in polar waters shall hold a Polar Ship Certificate issued under the Polar Code.

items.question: What is the main purpose of the MARPOL Convention?
choices: A. To regulate the construction of passenger ships
B. To prevent collisions between ships at sea
C. To prevent pollution from ships
D. To set minimum standards for seafarer training
items.correct_text: To prevent pollution from ships
items.evidence: MARPOL is the principal international convention aimed at preventing pollution of the marine environment by ships from operational or accidental causes.

items.question: Which MARPOL Annex addresses pollution by garbage from ships?
choices: A. Annex VI
B. Annex I
C. Annex II
D. Annex V
items.correct_text: Annex V
items.evidence: MARPOL Annex V contains regulations for the prevention of pollution by garbage from ships.

items.question: Which set of conditions applies to the discharge of oily bilge water outside a special area?
choices: A. 15 ppm or less, at anchor, at least 3 nautical miles from land
B. 100 ppm or less, proceeding en route, at least 25 nautical miles from land
C. 15 ppm or less, proceeding en route, at least 50 nautical miles from land
D. 50 ppm or less, proceeding en route, at least 12 nautical miles from land
items.correct_text: 15 ppm or less, proceeding en route, at least 50 nautical miles from land
items.evidence: Outside special areas, oily mixtures may be discharged only through approved equipment, with oil content not exceeding 15 ppm, while proceeding en route, and at least 50 nautical miles from the nearest land.

items.question: In a MARPOL Annex I special area, what is the general rule for oil discharges?
choices: A. Discharge of oil or oily mixtures is prohibited
B. Discharge at 15 ppm is always permitted
C. Discharge is permitted only during daylight hours
D. Discharge is permitted within 12 nautical miles of land
items.correct_text: Discharge of oil or oily mixtures is prohibited
items.evidence: In special areas, the discharge of oil or oily mixtures is generally prohibited, subject only to narrow exceptions.

items.question: Which operations are recorded in Oil Record Book Part I?
choices: A. Sewage treatment and discharge
B. Machinery-space bilge operations
C. Garbage discharges and incineration
D. Cargo and ballast operations of oil tankers
items.correct_text: Machinery-space bilge operations
items.evidence: Oil Record Book Part I covers machinery-space operations such as bilge water, sludge, and fuel-oil transfers; Part II covers cargo and ballast operations of oil tankers.

items.question: How long must an Oil Record Book be retained on board?
choices: A. 5 years
B. 3 years
C. 1 year
D. 2 years
items.correct_text: 3 years
items.evidence: The Oil Record Book shall be kept on board and retained for a period of three years.

items.question: Which ships must carry a Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP)?
choices: A. All ships of 100 gross tonnage and above
B. Oil tankers of 150 GT and other ships of 400 GT
C. Only oil tankers of 10,000 gross tonnage and above
D. Only passenger ships on international voyages
items.correct_text: Oil tankers of 150 GT and other ships of 400 GT
items.evidence: Oil tankers of 150 gross tonnage and above and all other ships of 400 gross tonnage and above shall carry a SOPEP.

items.question: What is the maximum oil content permitted in bilge water discharged through approved equipment?
choices: A. 15 ppm
B. 100 ppm
C. 30 ppm
D. 5 ppm
items.correct_text: 15 ppm
items.evidence: Approved oily-water separating equipment must ensure that the oil content of the effluent does not exceed 15 ppm.

items.question: Which oil tankers must be fitted with an oil discharge monitoring and control system?
choices: A. Oil tankers of 50 gross tonnage and above
B. Only oil tankers of 10,000 gross tonnage and above
C. Only oil tankers built after 2020
D. Oil tankers of 150 gross tonnage and above
items.correct_text: Oil tankers of 150 gross tonnage and above
items.evidence: Under MARPOL Annex I, Regulation 31, oil tankers of 150 gross tonnage and above shall be fitted with an oil discharge monitoring and control system.

items.question: Which noxious liquid substance category presents the greatest hazard under MARPOL Annex II?
choices: A. Category Y
B. Category Z
C. Category OS
D. Category X
items.correct_text: Category X
items.evidence: Category X substances present a major hazard to marine resources or human health and are subject to the strictest discharge controls.

items.question: Which document describes how a ship's noxious liquid cargo is handled and discharged?
choices: A. Garbage Management Plan
B. Oil Record Book Part I
C. Cargo Securing Manual and lashing plan
D. Procedures and Arrangements Manual
items.correct_text: Procedures and Arrangements Manual
items.evidence: A ship carrying noxious liquid substances in bulk shall have a Procedures and Arrangements Manual approved by the Administration.

items.question: Which record book is required for ships carrying noxious liquid substances in bulk?
choices: A. Cargo Record Book
B. Garbage Record Book
C. Oil Record Book Part I
D. Ballast Water Record Book
items.correct_text: Cargo Record Book
items.evidence: A Cargo Record Book shall be provided for ships carrying noxious liquid substances in bulk, and entries shall be retained for three years.

items.question: Which MARPOL Annex covers harmful substances carried in packaged form?
choices: A. Annex III
B. Annex II
C. Annex V
D. Annex I
items.correct_text: Annex III
items.evidence: MARPOL Annex III contains regulations for the prevention of pollution by harmful substances carried by sea in packaged form.

items.question: Outside how many nautical miles from the nearest land may untreated sewage be discharged?
choices: A. 50 nautical miles
B. 12 nautical miles
C. 6 nautical miles
D. 3 nautical miles
items.correct_text: 12 nautical miles
items.evidence: Untreated sewage may be discharged at a distance of more than 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, while proceeding en route at a speed of not less than 4 knots.

items.question: Sewage that is comminuted and disinfected using an approved system may be discharged at what minimum distance from land?
choices: A. 12 nautical miles
B. 1 nautical mile
C. 3 nautical miles
D. 50 nautical miles
items.correct_text: 3 nautical miles
items.evidence: Comminuted and disinfected sewage using an approved system may be discharged at a distance of more than 3 nautical miles from the nearest land, while proceeding en route at a speed of not less than 4 knots.

items.question: What must a ship have to discharge sewage within 3 nautical miles of land?
choices: A. A garbage management plan
B. A comminutor only
C. A holding tank only
D. A sewage treatment plant
items.correct_text: A sewage treatment plant
items.evidence: Within 3 nautical miles of land, sewage may be discharged only if the ship has an approved sewage treatment plant meeting the required effluent standard.

items.question: Which garbage may never be discharged into the sea under MARPOL Annex V?
choices: A. Cargo residues
B. Food waste
C. Cleaning agents
D. Plastic waste
items.correct_text: Plastic waste
items.evidence: The discharge of all plastics into the sea is prohibited, including synthetic ropes, fishing gear, and plastic bags.

items.question: Outside special areas, at what minimum distance may uncomminuted food waste be discharged?
choices: A. 25 nautical miles from nearest land
B. 3 nautical miles from nearest land
C. 12 nautical miles from nearest land
D. 6 nautical miles from nearest land
items.correct_text: 12 nautical miles from nearest land
items.evidence: Food waste not comminuted or ground may be discharged at least 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, while proceeding en route.

items.question: Comminuted food waste may be discharged at what minimum distance from land?
choices: A. 12 nautical miles from nearest land
B. 50 nautical miles from nearest land
C. 25 nautical miles from nearest land
D. 3 nautical miles from nearest land
items.correct_text: 3 nautical miles from nearest land
items.evidence: Comminuted or ground food waste capable of passing through a 25 mm screen may be discharged at least 3 nautical miles from the nearest land.

items.question: Cargo residues not harmful to the marine environment may be discharged outside how many nautical miles from land?
choices: A. 25 nautical miles
B. 50 nautical miles
C. 12 nautical miles
D. 3 nautical miles
items.correct_text: 12 nautical miles
items.evidence: Cargo residues that are not harmful to the marine environment may be discharged outside 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, subject to the Annex V conditions.

items.question: Which ships must carry a garbage management plan?
choices: A. Ships of 400 GT or certified for 15 persons
B. Only ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and above
C. All ships of 100 gross tonnage and above
D. Only passenger ships on international voyages
items.correct_text: Ships of 400 GT or certified for 15 persons
items.evidence: Every ship of 400 gross tonnage and above, and every ship certified to carry 15 persons or more, shall carry a garbage management plan.

items.question: How long must a Garbage Record Book be retained?
choices: A. 5 years
B. 1 year
C. 2 years
D. 3 years
items.correct_text: 2 years
items.evidence: The Garbage Record Book shall be kept on board and retained for a period of two years.

items.question: Which ships must display placards notifying persons of garbage disposal requirements?
choices: A. Ships of 400 gross tonnage and above
B. Ships of 12 metres or more in length
C. Ships of 24 metres or more in length
D. Ships of 100 metres or more in length
items.correct_text: Ships of 12 metres or more in length
items.evidence: Every ship of 12 metres or more in length shall display placards notifying crew and passengers of the garbage disposal requirements.

items.question: Which sea area is a MARPOL Annex V special area?
choices: A. The Mediterranean Sea
B. The South China Sea
C. The Bay of Bengal
D. The Gulf of Mexico
items.correct_text: The Mediterranean Sea
items.evidence: The Mediterranean Sea is listed as a special area under MARPOL Annex V, with stricter garbage discharge controls.

items.question: What is the global sulphur limit for fuel oil under MARPOL Annex VI?
items.evidence: The global sulphur content limit for fuel oil used on board ships is 0.50% m/m.

items.question: What is the sulphur limit for fuel oil in a MARPOL Annex VI Emission Control Area?
items.evidence: The sulphur content of fuel oil used in an Emission Control Area shall not exceed 0.10% m/m.

items.question: What must be recorded when a ship changes over fuel oil to comply with an ECA sulphur limit?
choices: A. Date, time, and position
B. Only the cargo manifest number
C. Only the fuel supplier's company name
D. Only the engine room temperature
items.correct_text: Date, time, and position
items.evidence: A fuel oil changeover procedure shall be recorded, including the date, time, and position of the changeover.

items.question: How long must a Bunker Delivery Note be retained on board?
choices: A. 2 years
B. 3 years
C. 5 years
D. 1 year
items.correct_text: 3 years
items.evidence: The Bunker Delivery Note shall be retained on board for a period of three years.

items.question: How long must the representative fuel oil sample be retained?
choices: A. 3 months
B. 6 months
C. 12 months
D. 24 months
items.correct_text: 12 months
items.evidence: The representative sample of fuel oil supplied to the ship shall be retained for at least 12 months.

items.question: Ships built on or after 1 January 2016 must meet which NOx tier when operating in a NOx Emission Control Area?
choices: A. Tier III
B. Tier II
C. Tier 0
D. Tier I
items.correct_text: Tier III
items.evidence: New ships built on or after 1 January 2016 and operating in a NOx Emission Control Area must comply with the Tier III NOx limit.

items.question: What does the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) measure?
choices: A. CO2 per tonne-mile of transport work
B. The sulphur content of fuel oil
C. The noise level of the main engine
D. The ballast water treatment capacity
items.correct_text: CO2 per tonne-mile of transport work
items.evidence: The EEDI is a design index expressing the energy efficiency of new ships as grams of CO2 per tonne-mile of transport work.

items.question: Which ships must keep a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP) on board?
choices: A. All ships of 100 gross tonnage and above
B. Only passenger ships of any size
C. Ships of 400 gross tonnage and above
D. Only tankers of 10,000 gross tonnage and above
items.correct_text: Ships of 400 gross tonnage and above
items.evidence: Every ship of 400 gross tonnage and above shall keep on board a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan.

items.question: Which ships are subject to the Carbon Intensity Indicator rating?
choices: A. All ships of 400 gross tonnage and above
B. Only tankers of 150 gross tonnage and above
C. Only new ships built after 2023
D. Cargo and passenger ships over 5,000 GT
items.correct_text: Cargo and passenger ships over 5,000 GT
items.evidence: The CII rating applies to cargo and passenger ships of 5,000 gross tonnage and above.

items.question: What is the MARPOL Annex VI rule on ozone-depleting substances?
choices: A. Ozone-depleting substances are regulated only in port
B. Deliberate emissions are prohibited
C. Ozone-depleting substances may be vented during maintenance
D. The rule applies only to oil tankers
items.correct_text: Deliberate emissions are prohibited
items.evidence: Deliberate emissions of ozone-depleting substances are prohibited, and systems containing such substances shall be maintained to prevent leakage.

items.question: What must a port State ensure under MARPOL?
choices: A. A repair yard in every port
B. Free bunkering for every visiting ship
C. A pilot on every visiting ship
D. Reception facilities for ship waste
items.correct_text: Reception facilities for ship waste
items.evidence: Parties shall ensure the provision of adequate reception facilities for ship-generated waste, without causing undue delay to ships.

items.question: What is the main purpose of the STCW Convention?
choices: A. To prevent pollution from ships
B. To regulate the carriage of dangerous goods
C. To set standards for training and certification
D. To set international standards for ship construction
items.correct_text: To set standards for training and certification
items.evidence: STCW establishes international standards of training, certification, and watchkeeping for seafarers.

items.question: What does a Certificate of Competency authorise a seafarer to do?
choices: A. Operate a ship without any watchkeeping duties
B. Work only in a shipyard or dry dock
C. Serve in a specified capacity on board a ship
D. Act as a port State control officer
items.correct_text: Serve in a specified capacity on board a ship
items.evidence: A Certificate of Competency is issued to a seafarer who meets the requirements to serve in the capacity specified in the certificate.

items.question: What is the minimum age for a Certificate of Competency?
choices: A. 21 years
B. 18 years
C. 16 years
D. 20 years
items.correct_text: 18 years
items.evidence: The minimum age for the issue of a Certificate of Competency is 18 years.

items.question: What is the maximum validity of a seafarer's medical certificate?
choices: A. 2 years
B. 6 months
C. 1 year
D. 5 years
items.correct_text: 2 years
items.evidence: A medical certificate shall be valid for a maximum period of two years, or one year for seafarers under 18 years of age.

items.question: Which four elements make up basic safety training?
choices: A. Personal survival, fire fighting, first aid, and social responsibility
B. Fire prevention, engine maintenance, medical care, and ship security
C. Personal survival, radar operation, cargo stowage, and bridge resource management
D. Elementary first aid, GMDSS operation, tanker familiarization, and polar training
items.correct_text: Personal survival, fire fighting, first aid, and social responsibility
items.source: STCW Regulation VI/1 and Code A-VI/1
items.evidence: Basic safety training comprises personal survival techniques, fire prevention and fire fighting, elementary first aid, and personal safety and social responsibilities.

items.question: What does personal survival techniques training cover?
choices: A. Cargo stowage and securing on deck
B. Survival at sea and life-saving appliances
C. Engine room maintenance procedures
D. Port State control inspection procedures
items.correct_text: Survival at sea and life-saving appliances
items.evidence: Personal survival techniques training covers survival at sea, abandonment procedures, and the use of life-saving appliances.

items.question: What does fire prevention and fire fighting training cover?
choices: A. Inspecting and repairing fire pumps ashore
B. Preventing, containing, and fighting fires on board
C. Designing ship fire detection systems
D. Investigating fires after the ship has been scrapped
items.correct_text: Preventing, containing, and fighting fires on board
items.evidence: Fire prevention and fire fighting training covers the causes of fire, fire prevention, and the use of fire-fighting equipment.

items.question: What does elementary first aid training cover?
choices: A. Cargo damage assessment and surveying
B. Advanced surgery and pharmaceutical prescribing
C. Basic first aid on board
D. Fire team leadership and incident command
items.correct_text: Basic first aid on board
items.evidence: Elementary first aid training provides basic knowledge and skills to give immediate first aid to injured or ill persons on board.

items.question: What does personal safety and social responsibilities training cover?
choices: A. Engine room watchkeeping and maintenance
B. Cargo documentation and charter party terms
C. Navigation plotting and collision avoidance
D. Safe working practices and emergency procedures
items.correct_text: Safe working practices and emergency procedures
items.evidence: Personal safety and social responsibilities training covers safe working practices, emergency procedures, and the social responsibilities of seafarers.

items.question: Which certificate is required to take charge of a survival craft or rescue boat?
choices: A. Basic safety training only
B. Medical first aid and advanced fire fighting
C. Advanced fire fighting
D. Survival craft and rescue boats
items.correct_text: Survival craft and rescue boats
items.evidence: Seafarers designated to take charge of survival craft or rescue boats must hold a certificate of proficiency in survival craft and rescue boats.

items.question: What does advanced fire fighting training cover?
choices: A. Directing fire-fighting operations on board
B. Cleaning and painting fire mains
C. Designing shore-side fire stations
D. Basic use of a single portable extinguisher
items.correct_text: Directing fire-fighting operations on board
items.evidence: Advanced fire fighting training covers the organisation, command, and direction of fire-fighting operations on board ship.

items.question: What does medical first aid training cover?
choices: A. Immediate first aid on board
B. Advanced medical care and diagnosis
C. GMDSS distress alerting procedures
D. Cargo surveying and damage assessment
items.correct_text: Immediate first aid on board
items.evidence: Medical first aid training covers the immediate first aid and emergency care of injured or ill persons on board.

items.question: What is the primary responsibility of the officer in charge of a navigational watch?
choices: A. Supervising cargo loading in the holds
B. Conducting port State control inspections
C. Safe navigation and a proper lookout
D. Maintaining the engine room logbook
items.correct_text: Safe navigation and a proper lookout
items.evidence: The officer in charge of the navigational watch is responsible for the safe navigation of the ship and for maintaining a proper lookout.

items.question: Which certificate is required for a seafarer operating GMDSS equipment in sea areas A1, A2, and A3?
choices: A. General Operator's Certificate
B. Restricted Operator's Certificate
C. Advanced fire fighting certificate
D. Basic safety training certificate
items.correct_text: General Operator's Certificate
items.evidence: The General Operator's Certificate is required for GMDSS radio operators in sea areas A1, A2, and A3.

items.question: Which training is required for officers using radar for collision avoidance?
choices: A. Tanker familiarization training
B. Radar and ARPA training
C. Medical care training
D. GMDSS radio training
items.correct_text: Radar and ARPA training
items.evidence: Officers in charge of a navigational watch must have completed approved radar and ARPA training.

items.question: Which training is required for officers using an Electronic Chart Display and Information System?
choices: A. ARPA training only
B. GMDSS training
C. ECDIS training
D. Proficiency in survival craft training
items.correct_text: ECDIS training
items.evidence: Officers using ECDIS must have completed approved ECDIS training.

items.question: What does Bridge Resource Management training cover?
choices: A. Cargo planning and stowage calculations
B. Port State control detention appeals
C. Effective bridge teamwork and communication
D. Engine room maintenance scheduling
items.correct_text: Effective bridge teamwork and communication
items.evidence: Bridge Resource Management training covers the effective use of all resources available to the bridge team, including teamwork, communication, and decision-making.

items.question: Which training is required for all seafarers under the ISPS Code?
choices: A. Medical care training
B. Proficiency in designated security duties
C. Security awareness training
D. Advanced fire fighting training
items.correct_text: Security awareness training
items.evidence: All seafarers shall receive security awareness training before being assigned to shipboard duties.

items.question: Which training is required for seafarers with designated security duties?
choices: A. Security awareness training only
B. Proficiency in designated security duties
C. Proficiency in survival craft and rescue boats
D. General Operator's Certificate
items.correct_text: Proficiency in designated security duties
items.evidence: Seafarers with designated security duties must complete proficiency in designated security duties training.

items.question: What does tanker familiarization training cover?
choices: A. Passenger ship crowd management
B. Polar navigation and icebreaking
C. Container terminal planning and operations
D. Basic tanker safety and operations
items.correct_text: Basic tanker safety and operations
items.evidence: Tanker familiarization training covers the basic safety and operational practices applicable to tankers.

items.question: Which training is required for seafarers on ships using gases or low-flashpoint fuels?
choices: A. IGF Code training
B. IMDG Code training
C. International Grain Code training
D. Polar Code training
items.correct_text: IGF Code training
items.evidence: Seafarers on ships subject to the IGF Code must complete appropriate IGF Code training.

items.question: Which training is required for masters and officers on ships operating in polar waters?
choices: A. General Operator's Certificate training
B. Tanker familiarization training
C. Advanced fire fighting training
D. Polar Code basic or advanced training
items.correct_text: Polar Code basic or advanced training
items.evidence: Masters, chief mates, and officers in charge of a navigational watch on ships operating in polar waters must complete basic or advanced Polar Code training.

items.question: What is the minimum rest period for a seafarer in any 24-hour period?
choices: A. 6 hours
B. 8 hours
C. 12 hours
D. 10 hours
items.correct_text: 10 hours
items.evidence: Seafarers shall be provided with a minimum of 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period.

items.question: What is the minimum rest period for a seafarer in any 7-day period?
choices: A. 91 hours
B. 84 hours
C. 70 hours
D. 77 hours
items.correct_text: 77 hours
items.evidence: Seafarers shall be provided with a minimum of 77 hours of rest in any 7-day period.

items.question: How may the minimum daily rest period be divided?
choices: A. Into no more than four periods of 2 hours
B. Two periods, one of at least 6 hours
C. Into one period of 10 hours only
D. Into any number of periods of any length
items.correct_text: Two periods, one of at least 6 hours
items.evidence: The rest period may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which shall be at least 6 hours, and the interval between consecutive rest periods shall not exceed 14 hours.

items.question: What is the main purpose of the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System?
choices: A. To manage cargo documentation between ports
B. To replace all shipboard navigation charts
C. To provide commercial satellite television for crews
D. Reliable distress and safety communications at sea
items.correct_text: Reliable distress and safety communications at sea
items.evidence: The GMDSS provides radiocommunication services for distress, urgency, safety, and maritime safety information.

items.question: What defines GMDSS sea area A1?
choices: A. An area outside all coast station coverage
B. An area within VHF coverage of at least one coast station
C. An area within MF coverage of at least one coast station
D. An area within Inmarsat satellite coverage
items.correct_text: An area within VHF coverage of at least one coast station
items.evidence: Sea area A1 is an area within radiotelephone coverage of at least one VHF coast station in which continuous DSC alerting is available.

items.question: What defines GMDSS sea area A2?
choices: A. An area within VHF coverage of at least one coast station
B. An area outside all coast station coverage
C. An area within MF coverage of at least one coast station
D. An area within Inmarsat satellite coverage
items.correct_text: An area within MF coverage of at least one coast station
items.evidence: Sea area A2 is an area within MF coverage of at least one coast station in which continuous DSC alerting is available.

items.question: What defines GMDSS sea area A3?
choices: A. An area within Inmarsat satellite coverage
B. An area outside all satellite coverage
C. An area within MF coverage of at least one coast station
D. An area within VHF coverage of at least one coast station
items.correct_text: An area within Inmarsat satellite coverage
items.evidence: Sea area A3 is an area within the coverage of an Inmarsat geostationary satellite in which continuous alerting is available.

items.question: What defines GMDSS sea area A4?
choices: A. An area within VHF coverage of at least one coast station
B. An area outside sea areas A1, A2, and A3
C. An area within Inmarsat satellite coverage
D. An area within MF coverage of at least one coast station
items.correct_text: An area outside sea areas A1, A2, and A3
items.evidence: Sea area A4 is an area outside sea areas A1, A2, and A3, generally the polar regions.

items.question: Which VHF channel is used for distress, urgency, safety, and calling?
choices: A. Channel 16
B. Channel 6
C. Channel 70
D. Channel 12
items.correct_text: Channel 16
items.source: SOLAS Chapter IV and ITU Radio Regulations
items.evidence: VHF Channel 16 is the international distress, urgency, safety, and calling channel.

items.question: Which VHF channel is used for Digital Selective Calling?
choices: A. Channel 16
B. Channel 70
C. Channel 12
D. Channel 6
items.correct_text: Channel 70
items.source: SOLAS Chapter IV and ITU Radio Regulations
items.evidence: VHF Channel 70 is reserved for Digital Selective Calling and shall not be used for voice communication.

items.question: What information does a DSC distress alert normally include?
choices: A. The crew list and next port of call
B. The cargo manifest and charter party details
C. The ship's insurance certificate number
D. MMSI, position, and distress nature
items.correct_text: MMSI, position, and distress nature
items.evidence: A DSC distress alert includes the vessel's identity, position, and the nature of the distress.

items.question: Which frequency does a satellite EPIRB use to alert the search and rescue system?
choices: A. 156.8 MHz
B. 518 kHz
C. 406 MHz
D. 121.5 MHz
items.correct_text: 406 MHz
items.evidence: A 406 MHz EPIRB transmits a distress alert to the COSPAS-SARSAT satellite system.

items.question: What does the float-free feature of an EPIRB mean?
choices: A. It transmits only when the ship is in port
B. It floats only when attached to a lifeboat
C. It must be manually switched on before every voyage
D. It activates automatically if the ship sinks
items.correct_text: It activates automatically if the ship sinks
items.evidence: A float-free EPIRB is designed to float free and activate automatically if the ship sinks.

items.question: Which frequency is used for homing on a 406 MHz EPIRB?
choices: A. 121.5 MHz
B. 406 MHz
C. 518 kHz
D. 9 GHz
items.evidence: EPIRBs transmit a low-power homing signal on 121.5 MHz for search aircraft and rescue vessels.

items.question: Which frequency does a search and rescue radar transponder use?
choices: A. 9 GHz
B. 121.5 MHz
C. 518 kHz
D. 406 MHz
items.correct_text: 9 GHz
items.evidence: A SART operates in the 9 GHz band and is detected by X-band radar.

items.question: How does a SART response appear on a radar display?
choices: A. As a continuous solid circle
B. As a series of radar dots
C. As a single stationary cross
D. As a numerical text message
items.correct_text: As a series of radar dots
items.evidence: A SART response appears on a radar display as a series of dots extending outward from the SART position.

items.question: Which frequency is used for international NAVTEX broadcasts?
choices: A. 9 GHz
B. 121.5 MHz
C. 518 kHz
D. 490 kHz
items.correct_text: 518 kHz
items.evidence: International NAVTEX broadcasts are made on 518 kHz in the English language.

items.question: Which frequency is used for national-language NAVTEX broadcasts?
choices: A. 518 kHz
B. 490 kHz
C. 406 MHz
D. 121.5 MHz
items.correct_text: 490 kHz
items.evidence: National NAVTEX broadcasts may be made on 490 kHz in the national language.

items.question: Which information is broadcast through NAVTEX?
choices: A. Commercial advertisements and port tariffs
B. Navigational and meteorological warnings and SAR information
C. Crew payroll and leave schedules
D. Cargo manifests and charter party terms
items.correct_text: Navigational and meteorological warnings and SAR information
items.evidence: NAVTEX broadcasts maritime safety information including navigational warnings, meteorological warnings, and search and rescue information.

items.question: What does the Enhanced Group Call system provide?
choices: A. Safety information broadcasts to sea areas
B. Automatic cargo tracking between ports
C. Private telephone calls between crew members
D. Television entertainment for passengers
items.correct_text: Safety information broadcasts to sea areas
items.evidence: The Enhanced Group Call system, such as SafetyNET, broadcasts maritime safety information to ships in selected sea areas.

items.question: What is Inmarsat used for in the GMDSS?
choices: A. Satellite communications for GMDSS
B. Radar detection of small targets
C. Electronic chart correction distribution
D. Automatic identification of nearby ships
items.correct_text: Satellite communications for GMDSS
items.evidence: Inmarsat provides satellite communication services used for GMDSS distress, urgency, and safety communications.

items.question: Which equipment provides DSC distress alerting on MF and HF?
choices: A. A NAVTEX receiver
B. A VHF handheld radiotelephone
C. A search and rescue radar transponder
D. An MF/HF radio installation with DSC
items.correct_text: An MF/HF radio installation with DSC
items.evidence: Ships in sea areas A3 and A4 carry an MF/HF radio installation with DSC for distress alerting and communications.

items.question: What must the GMDSS reserve source of energy be independent of?
choices: A. The ship's fire detection system
B. The ship's navigation lights
C. Propelling power and main power
D. The ship's steering gear
items.correct_text: Propelling power and main power
items.evidence: The reserve source of energy shall be independent of the propelling power and the ship's main electrical system.

items.question: Which record must be kept of GMDSS radiocommunications?
choices: A. An Oil Record Book
B. A Garbage Record Book
C. A Cargo Record Book
D. A radio log
items.correct_text: A radio log
items.evidence: A radio log shall be maintained to record GMDSS communications, including distress, urgency, and safety traffic.

items.question: Which certificate is required to operate GMDSS equipment in sea area A3?
choices: A. Restricted Operator's Certificate
B. Basic safety training certificate
C. Advanced fire fighting certificate
D. General Operator's Certificate
items.correct_text: General Operator's Certificate
items.evidence: The General Operator's Certificate is required for GMDSS operations in sea areas A1, A2, and A3.

items.question: When may a ship relay a distress alert from another vessel?
choices: A. Only when the distressed vessel is in the same port
B. Only after the distressed vessel has sunk
C. When direct communication is impossible
D. Never, because relaying is prohibited
items.correct_text: When direct communication is impossible
items.evidence: A distress relay may be sent when the station in distress cannot communicate directly with the rescue coordination centre or when further assistance is needed.

items.question: What should be done if a distress alert is transmitted accidentally?
choices: A. Switch off the radio and continue the voyage
B. Notify the coast station and cancel
C. Send a routine message to the next port
D. Wait for a rescue vessel to arrive
items.correct_text: Notify the coast station and cancel
items.source: SOLAS Chapter IV, Regulation 10 and ITU procedures
items.evidence: A false distress alert shall be cancelled immediately by notifying the appropriate coast station or rescue coordination centre.

items.question: Which distress signal has the highest priority in radiocommunications?
choices: A. A Securite safety signal
B. Routine traffic
C. A Mayday distress signal
D. A Pan Pan urgency signal
items.correct_text: A Mayday distress signal
items.source: ITU Radio Regulations and SOLAS Chapter IV
items.evidence: Mayday indicates grave and imminent danger and has priority over all other communications, followed by Pan Pan and Securite.

items.question: Which body is the port authority for Port Klang?
choices: A. Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency
B. Port Klang Authority
C. Malaysia Marine Department
D. Royal Malaysian Customs Department
items.correct_text: Port Klang Authority
items.evidence: Port Klang Authority is the port authority responsible for Port Klang.

items.question: Which two major container terminal operators operate in Port Klang?
choices: A. Tanjung Pelepas and Pasir Gudang
B. Northport and Westports
C. Kuantan Port and Kemaman Port
D. Penang Port and Johor Port
items.correct_text: Northport and Westports
items.evidence: Port Klang's main container terminals are operated by Northport (Malaysia) Bhd and Westports Malaysia Sdn Bhd.

items.question: Port Klang is a compulsory pilotage district. Which vessels are generally required to engage a licensed pilot?
choices: A. Only tankers above 200,000 deadweight tonnes
B. Only passenger ships on international voyages
C. Only vessels below 28 metres length overall
D. Vessels entering or leaving port limits
items.correct_text: Vessels entering or leaving port limits
items.evidence: All vessels entering, leaving, or navigating within the Port Klang pilotage district are required to engage a licensed pilot, subject to limited exemptions such as vessels below 28 metres LOA.

items.question: Which VHF channel is used to call Port Klang Traffic?
choices: A. Channel 70
B. Channel 6
C. Channel 12
D. Channel 16
items.correct_text: Channel 12
items.evidence: Vessels should call Port Klang Traffic on VHF Channel 12, with a listening watch also maintained on Channel 16.

items.question: How long before arrival should a vessel normally call Port Klang Traffic?
choices: A. 24 hours before arrival
B. 15 minutes before arrival
C. 2 hours before arrival
D. 30 minutes before arrival
items.correct_text: 2 hours before arrival
items.evidence: Vessels should call Port Klang Traffic on VHF Channel 12 two hours before arrival and provide the required arrival information.

items.question: What is the general speed limit for vessels navigating within Port Klang?
choices: A. 12 knots
B. 8 knots
C. 15 knots
D. 6 knots
items.correct_text: 12 knots
items.evidence: All vessels shall navigate at a safe speed and in no case exceed 12 knots within Port Klang.

items.question: What is the speed limit within 300 metres of wharves or mooring structures in Port Klang?
choices: A. 4 knots
B. 8 knots
C. 15 knots
D. 12 knots
items.correct_text: 8 knots
items.evidence: Vessels navigating within 300 metres of wharves or other mooring structures shall not exceed 8 knots.

items.question: Which system does Port Klang Authority operate to monitor vessel traffic in the port?
choices: A. Vessel Traffic Management System
B. Automatic Identification System only
C. STRAITREP reporting system
D. NAVTEX broadcast system
items.correct_text: Vessel Traffic Management System
items.evidence: Port Klang Authority operates a Vessel Traffic Management System for the pilotage district, using radar, AIS, VHF, and CCTV.

items.question: Which Malaysian agency is responsible for maritime search and rescue coordination?
choices: A. Royal Malaysian Customs Department
B. Malaysia Marine Department
C. Port Klang Authority
D. Maritime Enforcement Agency
items.correct_text: Maritime Enforcement Agency
items.evidence: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency is responsible for maritime search and rescue coordination in Malaysian waters.

items.question: Which regional port State control regime does Malaysia belong to?
choices: A. Paris MOU
B. Viña del Mar Agreement
C. Tokyo MOU
D. Caribbean MOU
items.correct_text: Tokyo MOU
items.evidence: Malaysia is a member authority of the Tokyo Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control in the Asia-Pacific Region.

items.question: What are the objectives of the ISM Code?
choices: A. Safety at sea and prevention of injury and environmental damage
B. Maximum cargo throughput, minimum port dues, and faster turnaround
C. Uniform crew wages, paid leave, and repatriation entitlements
D. Harmonised customs procedures and cargo documentation
items.correct_text: Safety at sea and prevention of injury and environmental damage
items.evidence: The objectives of the ISM Code are to ensure safety at sea, prevent human injury or loss of life, and avoid damage to the environment and to property.

items.question: What is a Safety Management System under the ISM Code?
choices: A. A documented safety and environmental management system
B. A list of cargo stowage positions for each voyage
C. A register of port State control deficiencies
D. A schedule of crew wages and leave entitlements
items.correct_text: A documented safety and environmental management system
items.evidence: A Safety Management System is a structured and documented system enabling company personnel to implement the company's safety and environmental policy.

items.question: What is the role of the Designated Person Ashore under the ISM Code?
choices: A. To command the ship when the master is absent
B. To conduct port State control inspections
C. To monitor safety and pollution prevention
D. To approve cargo securing manuals on behalf of the flag State
items.correct_text: To monitor safety and pollution prevention
items.evidence: The designated person ashore provides a direct link between the company and those on board and monitors the safety and pollution prevention aspects of the ship's operation.

items.question: What is the master's responsibility under the ISM Code?
choices: A. Negotiating charter parties with cargo owners
B. Implementing the SMS and motivating the crew
C. Designing the ship's cargo securing equipment
D. Preparing the company's annual financial statements
items.correct_text: Implementing the SMS and motivating the crew
items.evidence: The master is responsible for implementing the safety management system and for motivating the crew to observe it.

items.question: How often must internal safety audits be carried out under the ISM Code?
choices: A. At intervals not exceeding 5 years
B. At intervals not exceeding 12 months
C. At intervals not exceeding 3 months
D. At intervals not exceeding 6 months
items.correct_text: At intervals not exceeding 12 months
items.evidence: Internal audits shall be carried out at intervals not exceeding 12 months.

items.question: What is a non-conformity under the ISM Code?
choices: A. A commercial dispute between the owner and the charterer
B. A change of flag State during a voyage
C. Objective evidence of non-fulfilment of a requirement
D. A planned maintenance task that has been completed early
items.correct_text: Objective evidence of non-fulfilment of a requirement
items.evidence: A non-conformity is an observed situation where objective evidence indicates the non-fulfilment of a specified requirement.

items.question: What is a major non-conformity under the ISM Code?
choices: A. A serious threat requiring immediate corrective action
B. A delay in submitting the annual cargo report
C. A disagreement over the interpretation of a charter party clause
D. A minor documentation error that can be corrected at the next audit
items.correct_text: A serious threat requiring immediate corrective action
items.evidence: A major non-conformity is an identifiable deviation that poses a serious threat to the safety of personnel or the ship or a serious risk to the environment and requires immediate corrective action.

items.question: What does a Document of Compliance certify under the ISM Code?
choices: A. That the crew has completed security awareness training
B. That the ship has passed a port State control inspection
C. That a particular ship is seaworthy for its intended voyage
D. That the company's SMS complies with the ISM Code
items.correct_text: That the company's SMS complies with the ISM Code
items.evidence: A Document of Compliance is issued to a company that complies with the requirements of the ISM Code.

items.question: What does a Safety Management Certificate certify under the ISM Code?
choices: A. That the ship has completed an ISPS security drill
B. That the company's head office has been audited
C. That the ship has a valid cargo securing manual
D. That the ship follows its approved safety management system
items.correct_text: That the ship follows its approved safety management system
items.evidence: A Safety Management Certificate is issued to a ship to signify that the ship operates in accordance with the company's safety management system.

items.question: What is ISPS security level 1?
choices: A. An exceptional level applied when a security incident is probable or imminent
B. Normal level with minimum protective measures
